title: Equity transactions & liability classification — Oakmont Corp.
instructions: Oakmont Corp. (calendar year) had the equity and liability events below. Record the treasury stock reissuance, compute the equity amounts, and review the controller's draft note.

exhibits.title: Equity at January 1, Year 2
exhibits.content:
- Preferred stock, 6% cumulative, $100 par, **8,000** shares — $800,000 (dividends **one year in arrears**)
- Common stock, $5 par, **300,000** shares issued and outstanding — $1,500,000
- APIC — common: $2,400,000
- APIC — treasury stock: **$0**
- Retained earnings: $3,100,000

exhibits.title: Year 2 events
exhibits.content:
1. Mar 1: purchased **10,000** common shares as treasury stock at **$18**.
2. Jun 1: reissued **6,000** treasury shares at **$15**.
3. Nov 15: declared total cash dividends of **$150,000**, payable January 10.
4. Dec 31: net income **$620,000**.
5. A $500,000 note due May 1, Year 3 was refinanced on February 1, Year 3 (before the statements were issued) with a 4-year note of **$500,000**.

parts.prompt: Record the June 1 reissuance of treasury stock (cost method).
parts.explanation: Cash 6,000 × 15 = 90,000; cost 6,000 × 18 = 108,000. Shortfall 18,000; APIC–treasury stock has no balance, so retained earnings absorbs it. No loss account is ever used.

rows.label: Dividends allocated to preferred
rows.explanation: Annual preferred = 800,000 × 6% = 48,000. One year in arrears + current = **96,000**.

rows.label: Treasury stock balance at Dec 31 (enter as a positive number)

parts.prompt: Review the controller's draft note and correct any errors.

segments.text: The loss on reissuance of treasury stock was reported

options: as a reduction of retained earnings
segments.answer: as a reduction of retained earnings
segments.explanation: Treasury stock transactions never produce income statement gains or losses; with no APIC–treasury stock, the shortfall reduces retained earnings.

segments.text: . Preferred dividends in arrears at January 1 were

segments.original: recorded as a liability at the end of Year 1
options: recorded as a liability at the end of Year 1
disclosed in the notes at the end of Year 1
segments.answer: disclosed in the notes at the end of Year 1
segments.explanation: Arrears are disclosed, not accrued, until declared.

segments.text: . The $500,000 note due May 1, Year 3 is classified as

segments.explanation: It was refinanced on a long-term basis before the statements were issued.

segments.text: . The cash dividend declared November 15 is reported as

options: a reduction of retained earnings only when paid
segments.explanation: Correct as written: declaration creates a liability.
